paper_title: An unusual presentation of inhalation injury in a patient with high voltage electrical injury: A case report
disease_label_per_paper: high-voltage electrical injury with 45.5% TBSA burns, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome, renal failure, and inhalation injury
presentation_summary: A 20-year-old construction worker sustained electrical contact injury after a metal gutter contacted a transformer and overhead wires.
Electrothermal discharge ignited his clothing, producing mixed deep partial- and full-thickness burns over 45.5% TBSA.
He had prehospital pulseless ventricular dysrhythmia requiring CPR, defibrillation, intubation, and transfer to a burn center.

Arrival findings included mechanical ventilation, GCS 3T, tachycardia, circumferential full-thickness right lower extremity burn, severe acidemia, low bicarbonate, myoglobin-positive dark urine, and CK peak above 33000 U/L within 24 hours.
Early course was complicated by suspected limb compartment syndrome requiring fasciotomy and delayed grade III inhalation injury with acute hypoxic respiratory failure on post-burn day 3.
rankable_evidence_window: Use the high-voltage electrical exposure, clothing ignition/flame mechanism, initial TBSA/depth/anatomic distribution, cardiac arrest/intubation status, initial labs, myoglobinuria/rhabdomyolysis, early compartment syndrome evidence, and post-burn day 3 bronchoscopy-proven inhalation injury. Do not use final discharge recovery, amputation, grafting sequence, tracheostomy timing, or retrospective discussion for ranking.
